conclusion.proposed_resolution: the Mexica day began at noon rather than at midnight
conclusion.consequence: a single European calendar day can correspond to two adjacent tonalpohualli days depending on the time of the event
conclusion.consequence_for_births: a birth whose recorded time is before local noon and one after it fall on different tonalpohualli days under this resolution
conclusion.status: an author's proposed resolution, not an established fact

conclusion.label: Tena, 26 February year start
conclusion.anchor_statement: The xiuhpohualli year begins on 26 February, on the day 1 Atlcahualo.
conclusion.notes: The consulted survey reports the tonalpohualli count as displaced by seven days relative to Caso, and reports no secondary correction. Neither the displacement nor the year-start rule can be encoded as an anchor until Tena's own statement is obtained.

conclusion.label: Nuttall-Ochoa, equinox-locked with intercalation
conclusion.attributed_to: Zelia Nuttall, developed by Ruben Ochoa
conclusion.anchor_statement: Caso's 1 Coatl date is retained, an intercalary correction is applied, and 1 Cipactli is placed exactly one day after the observable spring equinox.
conclusion.notes: An observational rule, not a fixed day count: the anchor moves with the observed equinox, so it cannot be reduced to a single JDN offset. Recorded as a candidate family, not as an applicable profile.

conclusion.label: Meza, fixed Cipactli year start
conclusion.anchor_statement: The new year begins on the day Cipactli every year.
conclusion.notes: A fixed Cipactli year start cannot hold across a 365-day year against a 260-day count, because 365 is not a multiple of 20. Recorded so the candidate set is complete and so the incompatibility is on the record.
